actions.description: Upload an Opentrons protocol file that the operator overlay allows, create a run and send the robot's play action; the run continues on the robot after this action returns, until it ends or is stopped, and the protocol alone decides what the robot does in it

inputs.description: Path on the driver host of the Opentrons protocol file to upload; one of the paths the operator overlay allows
inputs.name: protocol_path

actions.name: start_protocol

outputs.description: Identifier assigned to the uploaded protocol
outputs.name: protocol_id

outputs.description: Identifier assigned to the created run
outputs.name: run_id

outputs.description: Run status reported by the robot right after it accepted the play action
outputs.name: status

actions.description: Send the robot's run stop action to every run it lists as running, paused, finishing or in a status the clone does not name, and to a run of this driver whose play may be in flight, and confirm each by a fresh read; it takes no input
actions.name: stop_active_run

outputs.description: Runs that received the stop action, each confirmed; empty when no run needed one
outputs.name: stopped_runs

outputs.description: Status a fresh read reported after the stop action
outputs.name: stopped_runs[*].status

facts.text: The module is a MADSci node for Opentrons liquid handlers, the OT-2 and the Flex
OT2_Driver builds the robot base URL from config.ip and config.port and sets the Opentrons-Version: 2 request header
The constructor probes /robot/lights and raises RuntimeError when the probe does not return HTTP 200
After the probe the constructor switches the robot lights on; when the probe does not report them off it first switches them off and sleeps one second
change_lights_status posts {'on': status} to /robot/lights

transfer opens the local protocol file, posts it to /protocols with timeout=600, prints the answer's status code, text and reason, creates a run at /runs with timeout=60 and returns the protocol id and run id
resume posts actionType 'play' to /runs/{run_id}/actions without a timeout and returns the response without checking its status code
cancel posts actionType 'stop' to /runs/{run_id}/actions without a timeout and returns the response without checking its status code
execute compares the answer of the play action with 201, which it calls the good response code for this endpoint, and only prints when it differs
execute posts play and polls check_run_status every second, catching and printing every exception, until the run is failed, succeeded or stopped
RunStatus names idle, running, finishing, succeeded, failed, paused, stop-requested and stopped
check_run_status reads /runs/{run_id}, prints when the answer is not HTTP 200 and constructs RunStatus from the response data.status
get_run returns the JSON of GET /runs/{run_id} and only prints when the answer is not HTTP 200

get_runs sends GET /runs without a timeout, maps the id, protocolId, status and current of each run in its data list to runID, protocolID, status and current, and returns None when /runs does not answer HTTP 200

get_robot_status returns 'offline' when get_runs returns None, skips succeeded and stop-requested runs, returns the status of the first other run whose status RunStatus names, and returns 'idle' when none does
reset_robot_data sends DELETE /runs/{runID} for every run whose status is failed
send_request joins base_url and the request extension, sets the Opentrons-Version: 2 header when no headers are given, requires a method keyword and passes the keyword arguments to requests.request
The protocol generator's Temperature_Set command sets a temperature module to an integer change_temp
The protocol generator's Move_Labware command moves labware inside the Flex with the gripper
OT2Node.execute sets self.run_id to the run id before OT2_Driver.execute and back to None after it returns
OT2Node.execute answers a run whose status is stopped with the message that the OT2 is successfully IDLE after stopping a protocol
OT2Node.safety_stop logs and sets node_status.stopped; it sends no stop to the robot
OT2Node.cancel logs and calls self.ot2_interface.cancel(self.run_id)

measures.description: The upstream get_robot_status(): the status of the first run in the robot's list that is not succeeded or stop-requested (an older stopped or failed run can hide a newer running one; read runs for every run), offline when /runs does not answer HTTP 200, idle when no run matches
measures.name: robot_status

measures.description: All runs stored on the robot; the read fails when /runs does not answer HTTP 200
measures.name: runs

measures.description: Identifier of the run most recently created through this driver (kept after the run ends or is stopped); empty when none
measures.name: active_run_id

measures.description: Status the robot reports for the run most recently created through this driver, or idle when there is none
measures.name: active_run_status

operator_required.name: start_protocol
operator_required.reason: Which protocol files may run is the operator's decision: a protocol decides the volumes, labware, modules and motion of its run, the clone uploads it unchecked (src/ot2_interface/ot2_driver_http.py:146-158) and names no protocol or directory a deployment may run. The overlay lists the approved paths as an allowed set.

safe_state.description: Every run the robot lists as running, paused, finishing or in a status the clone's RunStatus does not name, and a new run of this driver whose play may be in flight, got the run stop action and then read stop-requested, stopped, succeeded or failed (stop-requested: the stop was accepted, motion may not have ended); a run stop over the HTTP API, not a hardware stop: it neither resets module set points nor stops anything outside a run, and no run is started
